title: Staying out of artists' contract business; his own business naivete
summary: He avoided advising artists on contracts after rejections, says no one understood how much good royalties could earn, and admits he lacked capital sense even with Dover.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Did you become... Did you become... When record companies did come down here and were, I'd say, offering bad contracts, so to speak, I mean, some were... Well... Did you become... Did you become... I say a middleman? Or did you become...

I didn't get too involved in people's business because, strangely enough, most of them would reject any kind of, let me pull you over in a corner and put my arm on your shoulder and get you wise to something kind of thing. Right. I tried that, you know, enough times that... And got enough rejections that I pretty much didn't do it, you know? Uh-huh. Uh-huh. People wanted to make that record and it kind of blinded them to them.
even though the deal may have been well let's put it

a lot of people thought for instance that no matter what the record company paid them if they had a hit record they'd go out on the road and make money with their appearances and things like that and I don't think any of us even me understood the enormity of the money that you could make with good royalties on a really big selling record and so it was late blooming and even when I did start it I wasn't as good a businessman as I should have been or could have been and I didn't bring in that kind of expertise when I had Dover Records even when I was selling a lot of records there wasn't a lot of good business practice going on you know there were a few things I understood and I did those hopefully right but the accumulation of capital the leveraging of capital I never thought in those terms I do now I think about it and I know about it
and I wasn't any spring chicken by then I'd been around a while you know but I really was kind of naive
of the larger view of the record business

well yeah of business even you know I think record or what you know I wasn't a good businessman frankly and it's no fun I have to say that but I think if I'm going to be honest about it you know that can be candid but I generally try to be candid you know nobody's perfect but hell I am I try to be
